items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: like, say, Sister Kate. But let's see, the last Sister Kate, though, that they mastered... turned out to be one of the best ones.

ctx.x: But wasn't, I mean, would you say you recorded quite a bit of the total that was recorded of him?

Oh, possibly. A lot of other people recorded him. But maybe in total number of sides. Of course, now they've been reissuing, or not only reissuing, but also issuing some new material in Japan. Second masters and rejects and all, I would have called them. Some of those rejects aren't any worse than the first ones, really. And some of them are actually pretty good at times. And there's hardly an excuse to issue four or five masters of one tune, like, say, Sister Kate. But let's see, the last Sister Kate, though,…
There wasn't any soloing as such then. Was there a soloing of instruments? It was all purely on sound.
